title: Junior Project Controls (00523)

title: Junior Scheduler / Project Controls Consultant
description: SOCOTEC is a provider of niche consulting services within the architecture, engineering and construction industries focusing on high-performance buildings and specialty structures. Develop and update Critical Path Method (CPM) schedules based on project scope, construction sequencing, and contractor work plans. Support preparation of baseline schedules, schedule updates, recovery schedules, and short-term look-ahead schedules. Review contractor schedule submissions for completeness, logic, sequencing, durations, and compliance with project requirements. Monitor project progress and incorporate actual progress into schedule updates. Identify critical and near-critical activities, schedule constraints, and potential impacts to project milestones. Assist with analysis of schedule variances and changes to the critical path. Work with project teams to collect schedule information, progress data, and supporting documentation. Assist in preparing schedule narratives, progress reports, schedule graphics, and management presentations. Support schedule impact assessments and preliminary delay analyses under the direction of senior scheduling and claims professionals. Assist with evaluating change orders and potential time impacts. Review project documentation, including drawings, specifications, contracts, progress reports, RFIs, submittals, and change documentation, to understand project sequencing and schedule impacts. Participate in project meetings and schedule review meetings with clients, contractors, designers, and other project stakeholders. Support broader project controls activities, including progress measurement, reporting, cost and schedule integration, and project performance analysis. Maintain clear and organized documentation supporting schedule updates and analyses. Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, Construction Engineering, Architecture, or a related field. Approximately 2 or more years of relevant construction industry experience, preferably working for a general contractor, construction manager, or specialty contractor. Practical experience developing or maintaining construction schedules. Understanding of construction sequencing, project milestones, and the relationship between design, procurement, and construction activities. Basic understanding of Critical Path Method (CPM) scheduling principles. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to organize and analyze project information and communicate findings clearly. Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint. Ability to work collaboratively as part of a multidisciplinary project team. Preferred Experience using Oracle Primavera P6. Experience with Microsoft Project or other scheduling/project controls software. Experience working on commercial buildings, healthcare, higher education, transportation, infrastructure, or other complex construction projects. Exposure to schedule review, delay analysis, change-order evaluation, or construction claims. Familiarity with construction drawings, specifications, contracts, and project documentation. Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification or interest in pursuing professional certification is a plus. Ideal Candidate The ideal candidate has started their career working directly within the construction industry and understands how projects are actually planned and built. They have had hands-on exposure to construction scheduling and are interested in developing deeper expertise in project controls, schedule analysis, and construction advisory . This position is particularly well suited to someone who has spent the first few years of their career with a contractor or construction manager and is interested in transitioning into a consulting environment where they can work across multiple projects, clients, and construction sectors. What You Will Develop In this role, you will have the opportunity to develop expertise in: Advanced CPM scheduling Primavera P6 Construction schedule review and analysis Project controls and performance reporting Schedule risk and critical path analysis Change and delay analysis Construction claims and dispute support Project advisory and owner representation You will work alongside experienced construction, engineering, scheduling, and project controls professionals and gain exposure to complex projects from both the contractor and owner perspectives. For more information, please visit www.socotec.us Job Type: Full Time (4 days a week in office with one hybrid/ remote day) The position may be based in our Atlanta, New York, or Boston office. Some travel to project sites and client offices may be required depending on project assignments. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. description: ABOUT FLUIDSTACK We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward. - Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world. THE CONSTRUCTION TEAM Examples of key problems the team is working on - Put gigawatts in the ground, faster than anyone has. We're delivering one of the largest data center buildouts of its kind, with many sites running at once. Traditional construction management breaks at this scale, so we're building the model that replaces it. - Throw out traditional construction and invent how gigawatts get built. Tons of tools, layers of process, and administrative drag don't get you there. You'll strip all of that out and win by solving the real problem and beating the goal, not by managing toward it. - Productize the data center so we can build it a thousand times. You'll turn one-off construction into a repeatable, modular build, where the hundredth site goes up faster and cleaner than the first. That repeatability is the only way to reach the scale we're targeting.   • Familiarity with regional carrier networks and basic domestic shipping regulations.
  • Experience in a fulfillment, warehouse, or logistics coordination role, ideally within a high-growth e-commerce environment.

title: Project Manager, IPP
description:
New Leaf Energy is an experienced clean energy developer that partners with landowners, policymakers, and other stakeholders to accelerate the transition to a world powered by renewable energy. We identify high-value sites, work with landowners and local communities to develop them, and partner with long-term asset owners to bring the most impactful clean energy projects to life.

Position Summary 

The Project Manager, IPP (“PM”) is responsible for the day-to-day execution of projects during construction and commissioning. This role manages contractors, schedules, budgets, and site activities to ensure projects are executed safely, efficiently, and in alignment with approved plans. The PM operates within established cost, schedule, and technical frameworks and escalates risks, changes, and issues in accordance with the IPP’s organizational and governance structures.

Position responsibilities will include, but are not limited to: 

Project Execution

  • Lead day-to-day execution of assigned projects to commercial operation.
  • Serve as the IPP’s primary point of contact for EPC contractors, major suppliers, and third-party inspectors during construction, escalating commercial disputes or high-impact technical issues
  • Support commissioning, performance testing, and punch-list resolution.
  • Prepare and organize COD documentation and turnover materials.
  • Review EPC Contractor and vendor compliance with PWA, insurance, and other contract requirements
  • Identify and document contractor performance issues or contract deviations, escalating to senior leadership for formal notice preparation and resolution
  • Assist in organizing commissioning schedules, tracking punch-list items to completion, and compiling turnover documentation for the Asset Management team.

Schedule, Cost, and Reporting

  • Maintain and update detailed project schedules and construction plans.
  • Track weekly project expenditures against approved budget, update progress tracking models, and review contractor invoices against progress tracking models. 
  • Prepare accurate, timely project reports for senior leadership, lenders, and internal stakeholders.
  • Identify schedule and cost risks early and escalate with clear documentation and recommendations.

Change Management

  • Identify potential changes in scope, cost, or schedule and initiate change orders.
  • Coordinate technical evaluation with the Director of Engineering and commercial review with senior leadership.
  • Log potential change orders, collect backup documentation (cost estimates, schedule impacts) from contracts, and support senior management in reviewing change order packages. 
  • Implement approved changes and track execution impacts.

Quality, Safety and Compliance

  • Conduct routine site visits, safety observations, and progress verification.
  • Coordinate factory acceptance testing logistics, schedules, and documentation with vendors, EPCs, and Engineering.
  • Escalate safety incidents, near misses, and unsafe conditions.
  • Support incident investigations and corrective action implementation in coordination with senior leadership and contractors.

Desired Qualifications 

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or related field.
  • At least three years of renewable energy construction or project management experience (IPP or EPC).
  • Strong understanding of construction sequencing, contractor management, and site safety.
  • Experience supporting change management and contract administration.
  • Excellent communication, organization, and escalation judgment.

 

Compensation

New Leaf Energy compensates all employees in three ways: market-competitive base salary, plus above-market variable compensation, plus an equity-like program such that all employees experience the benefits of ownership.  We use a data-driven and transparent methodology to calibrate compensation that is externally competitive and internally equitable, guided by the New Leaf Energy compensation manual, which is available to all employees.

Under our compensation framework, the likely base salary range for this position in the Boston location is $117,043 - 136,939. The on-target annual cash bonus associated with this position is an additional 10% percent of base salary. Your actual salary may be above, in, or below this range, depending on your location and experience.

We value transparency and can share more during the interview process.

 

Benefits and Culture

New Leaf Energy’s success is driven by our collaborative, long-term relationships based on trust and transparency. We offer a flexible work environment that places significant responsibility in independent teams and creates opportunities for innovation and personal growth. New Leaf Energy’s benefits are designed to appropriately recognize our employees’ contributions and enable a reasonable work/life balance. Our benefits include:

  • Competitive salaries and comprehensive benefits, including medical, dental and vision;
  • A 401k plan with immediate vesting and a company match (100% of the first three percent of your pay; 50% for the next two percent you contribute);
  • An open and self-managed paid time-off policy;
  • A hybrid work location policy that supports working from home for part of the week;
  • A parental leave policy for both birthing and non-birthing parents, available immediately upon hire;
  • Professional development and education assistance.

Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

New Leaf Energy values the diverse perspectives, skills, experiences, and contributions of all employees. We want all our employees to feel like they belong and are empowered to be their most authentic selves at work. We’re actively committed to fostering diversity and creating an inclusive environment not only within our own organization but also within the clean energy industry.

We seek a diverse candidate pool in this–and every–search. New Leaf Energy provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender, age, sexual orientation, national origin, ancestry, disability, genetics, veteran status or any other characteristic protected by state, federal and local laws. In addition to federal law requirements, New Leaf Energy complies with applicable state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment in every location in which the company has facilities. EEO M/F/D/V.

A Note to Third-Party Recruiters

New Leaf Energy’s People + Culture team coordinates all recruiting and hiring at our company. New Leaf Energy does not accept unsolicited resumes from third-party recruiters, staffing firms, or related agencies. Resumes are only accepted from third-party recruiters, staffing firms, or related agencies if a signed agreement is in place AND if external recruiting assistance is authorized by the People + Culture team for a specific position. All unsolicited resumes will be considered the property of New Leaf Energy. New Leaf Energy is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

Availability during the team’s Eastern Time workday. Helpful, not required Experience with Linear, GitHub, Slack, Next.js, or TypeScript. Experience with consumer web forms, multi-brand products, compliance-sensitive changes, affiliate marketing, or partner integrations. Experience using LLM-assisted development tools in a controlled review and release process. How the team works You report to the Engineering Lead and work directly with engineers and stakeholders. Engineers own feature implementation. You own clarity, coordination, and delivery, with room to handle smaller technical changes yourself. Real Chemistry is looking for a Project Manager to join our growing Medical Affairs team!  

The Project Manager is responsible for delivering assigned medical affairs projects from initiation through final closeout, including planning, coordination, budget management, routing, approvals, and launch of project deliverables. Projects may include slide decks, print projects, congress materials, advisory board materials, scientific communications, and smaller digital initiatives. This role serves as a main point of contact across internal and external teams, partnering closely with Account, Scientific/Medical, Editorial, Creative, Studio, Print Production, User Experience, Technology, and Quality Assurance partners to keep work on time, on budget, and aligned to client expectations.

Whether it’s bringing in the right resources at the right time, aligning priorities with the account team, or identifying bottlenecks and proposing solutions early, no two days are the same.  

This is a hybrid role, based in any of our US offices—including New York City, Boston, Chicago or Indianapolis—or remotely within the US, depending on team and business needs. This role will primarily work Eastern business hours.

What you’ll do:  

  • Clearly communicate expectations to internal teams and vendors to support the efficient flow of work throughout the agency.
  • Partner with key agency teams to ensure projects stay on track and agreed-upon milestones are met, including Account, Scientific/Medical, Editorial, Creative, Studio, Print Production, Strategic Planning, Information UX, Technology, and Programming teams.

  • Collaborate with finance and accounting teams on revenue recognition/invoicing processes

  • Perform risk planning and mitigation to minimize project risk.

  • Route deliverables to appropriate core team members for review and signoff via the electronic project routing system.  
  • Ensure signoff prior to key milestones, including core team review, medical/scientific review, client review, vendor handoff, and final release.
  • Develop detailed work plans, schedules, and status reports to keep internal teams, clients, and external partners aligned throughout the project life cycle. 
  • Serve as a day-to-day project lead, helping define scope and objectives while motivating cross-functional teams to deliver high-quality work on time and on budget. 
  • Coordinate project deliverables from concept through delivery, ensuring the appropriate internal departments, reviews, approvals, and handoffs are engaged at each stage. 
  • Support adherence to agency process and manage the quality assurance phase for all projects.

This position is a perfect fit for you if:  

  • Our Company values – Best Together, Impact-Obsessed, Excellence Expected, Evolve Always and Accountability with an “I” – really speak to you.
  • You are adaptable, resilient, and OK with adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and focus as we grow. When things change, so do we. We’re always evolving.
  • You are proactive, driven, and resourceful with strong prioritization skills and a desire to dive into the data.
  • You are a highly organized self-starter who can work independently and manage tight deadlines.

What you should have:  

  • 3+ years of Project/Program Management or relevant experience. 
  • 2+ years of experience in budget management. 
  • Working familiarity with industry-specific processes, including medical, legal, regulatory, and client review.
  • Background working on teams focused on medical affairs, scientific communications, medical education, or related non-promotional healthcare communications projects.
  • Demonstrated track record of leading small- to medium-scale projects from conception through completion. 
  • Experience working cross-functionally with medical/scientific, editorial, account, creative, and project management partners to deliver high-quality products and services. 
  • Proficient in creating timelines and tracking progress against schedules.
  • Ability to communicate clearly and concisely with technical and non-technical teams across multiple business areas; excellent written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal skills.
